# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 49

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 49:1 "ministers" vs. "servants entrusted with"

- **EMET:** "who are the ministers of these commandments"
- **LOGOS:** "who are the ministers of these commandments"
- **PNEUMA:** "who are the servants entrusted with these commandments"
- **Greek:** *hoi leitourgoi tōn entolōn* — the ministers/liturgical servants of the commandments
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "who are the ministers of these commandments." EMET and LOGOS agree; *leitourgos* is a cultic/official service term; "ministers" preserves this better than PNEUMA's descriptive phrase.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 49:1 "I am not adding anything of my own" vs. "I am adding nothing of my own"

- **EMET:** "I am not adding anything of my own here"
- **LOGOS:** "I am adding nothing of my own here"
- **PNEUMA:** "I'm not adding anything of my own here"
- **Greek:** *ouk prosthētō ti ap' emautou* — I am not adding anything from myself
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "I am adding nothing of my own here" (LOGOS). "Adding nothing" is a stronger denial than "not adding anything."

---

## Disagreement 3 — 49:2 "die the death" vs. "will die" vs. "will face death"

- **EMET:** "he shall die the death"
- **LOGOS:** "he will die the death"
- **PNEUMA:** "they will face death"
- **Greek:** *apothaneitai* — he/she will die (simple future)
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "will die the death" (LOGOS). The doubled death formula "die the death" (*apothaneitai thanatō*) — if present in the Greek — echoes the Septuagint formula; PNEUMA's "face death" is too soft.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 49:2 "his works do not allow" vs. "his deeds do not permit"

- **EMET:** "because his works do not allow him to live"
- **LOGOS:** "for his deeds do not permit him to live"
- **PNEUMA:** "because the way they live doesn't allow them to live at all"
- **Greek:** *ta erga autou ouk aphiousin auton zēn* — his works do not allow him to live
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "for his deeds do not permit him to live" (LOGOS). "Deeds" and "permit" are slightly more precise than "works" and "allow" in this judicial context.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 49:3 "remain in the wretched condition" vs. "stay stuck in the miserable condition"

- **EMET:** "shall remain in the wretched condition in which they are"
- **LOGOS:** "will remain in the wretched state in which they find themselves"
- **PNEUMA:** "will stay stuck in the miserable condition they're already in"
- **Greek:** *en tē talaipōria autōn menousin* — they will remain in their wretchedness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "will remain in the wretched state in which they find themselves" (LOGOS). "State" is appropriate; PNEUMA's "stuck" adds a colloquial gloss.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 49:3 "good desire leads to life...evil desire leads to death" — all agree substantially

- **EMET:** "every good desire leads to life and every evil desire leads to death"
- **LOGOS:** "every good desire leads to life and every evil desire leads to death"
- **PNEUMA:** "every good desire points toward life, and every evil desire points toward death"
- **Note:** Minor variation on "leads" vs. "points toward"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "every good desire leads to life and every evil desire leads to death." EMET and LOGOS agree; "leads to" is more direct than "points toward."

---

## Disagreement 7 — 49:4 "hold fast to the good desire" vs. "hold on to good desire"

- **EMET:** "guard the good desire and keep it"
- **LOGOS:** "hold fast to the good desire and keep it"
- **PNEUMA:** "hold on to good desire and maintain it"
- **Greek:** *krateī tēn epithumian tēn agathēn* — hold/grasp/keep the good desire
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "hold fast to the good desire and keep it" (LOGOS). *Kratein* = to grasp firmly/hold fast — "hold fast" is most precise.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 49:4 "lest it depart from you" vs. "don't let it slip away"

- **EMET:** "so that it may not depart from you"
- **LOGOS:** "lest it depart from you"
- **PNEUMA:** "don't let it slip away"
- **Greek:** *mēpote apolthai apo sou* — lest it go away from you
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "lest it depart from you" (LOGOS). "Lest" introduces the purpose clause properly; "slip away" (PNEUMA) suggests passivity not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 49:5 "not the words of a man" vs. "not the words of a human being"

- **EMET:** "not the words of a man but of the Lord God"
- **LOGOS:** "not the words of a human being but of the Lord God"
- **PNEUMA:** "not a human being's words — they are the words of the Lord God"
- **Greek:** *ouk anthrōpou eisin alla tou kyriou theou* — they are not of a man but of the Lord God
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "not the words of a human being but of the Lord God" (LOGOS). "Human being" is more precise than "man" in this categorical contrast.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 49:5 "I have the authority to give such commandments"

- **EMET:** "I have the authority to give such commandments"
- **LOGOS:** "I have the authority to give such commandments"
- **PNEUMA:** "I have the authority to give commandments like these"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree exactly.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "I have the authority to give such commandments." The claim *exousian echō* = I have authority/power — a direct assertion of divine commission.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 49.*
